linkedin.title: I started building a news app when I was a teenager because I was tired of missing the stories that actually mattered.
linkedin.body:
The problem with the news today is not a lack of information. It is the overwhelming flood of it. Every day, thousands of articles are published, but most of them are noise. I wanted to build something that cut through that noise without relying on the same old editorial gatekeepers.

Building an AI-powered app at a young age taught me one big lesson. Technology is only useful if it respects the user. Too many apps are designed to keep you scrolling as long as possible. We took a different path. We focused on building a tool that learns what you care about and delivers it efficiently so you can get informed and get on with your day.

Personalisation is often treated like a buzzword. For us, it is a utility. It means you stop seeing headlines about things you do not care about and start seeing the context you need to understand the world. It is about giving you back your time.
linkedin.cta: If you are ready for a cleaner way to stay informed, you can see how we are doing it at HEADLINNE.com.

reels.hook: TikTok reaches $400 million settlement with US Justice Department over children’s privacy

beats.caption: TikTok reaches $400 million settlement with US Justice Department over children’s privacy
That is enough money to build a new stadium.
beats.narration: That is enough cash to build a brand new professional sports stadium from the ground up.

beats.caption: TikTok just settled a massive privacy lawsuit.
beats.narration: But that money isn't for a stadium. It is going to the US government.

beats.caption: They allegedly violated children's privacy laws.
beats.narration: The Justice Department sued them for breaking federal rules about how they handle kids' data.

beats.caption: This deal ends the long legal battle.
beats.narration: This settlement officially puts that 2024 lawsuit to rest.

beats.caption: It sends a serious message to tech giants.
beats.narration: It is a clear signal that federal regulators are watching how platforms treat our data.

beats.caption: Expect tighter scrutiny on app security.
beats.narration: Companies are now on notice that privacy violations come with a very high price tag.

story_card.headline: Why atoms emit mysterious gamma rays
story_card.standfirst: Scientists have finally cracked a decades-old physics puzzle about atomic behavior.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Researchers found that protons and neutrons inside atoms flip their internal magnets.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: For decades, experts were baffled by why some atomic nuclei release bursts of low-energy gamma rays.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: This discovery helps scientists create much more accurate models of how atoms function.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Future research will apply these findings to refine our broader understanding of nuclear physics.

story_card.caption:
Scientists have solved the mystery behind why some atomic nuclei unexpectedly release low-energy gamma rays.

By tracing the effect to magnetic flips inside the nucleus, researchers have unlocked a new piece of the physics puzzle. This breakthrough clarifies atomic behavior that has puzzled labs for decades. It is a big step forward for nuclear modeling.

Does learning about the hidden mechanics of atoms change how you view the physical world?
